correctness.rationale: Under i.i.d. atomless entries, all 9! rank permutations of 3×3 cells have probability 1/9!. The row minima and column maxima uniquely determine a six-vertex functional digraph. The rank-constrained linear-extension recurrence L(S)=sum over available cells of L(S∪{cell}) exhausts every rank order and correctly counts each of 3^6 possible map pairs, including zero-count inconsistent pairs. Independently enumerated all 362880 permutations in the working container, not merely read a recorded VERIFY_OK: joint (cycle type, max depth) counts were (2,1):9576,(2,2):69264,(2,3):22464,(2,4):6912,(4,1):127872,(4,2):110592,(6,0):15552,(2+4,0):648, summing 9!. Weighted counts of six vertex depths were (1267488,625536,247968,29376,6912), summing 6×9!, so P(T=0..4)=(163/280,181/630,41/360,17/1260,1/315) and E[T]=179/315. Summing by maximum gives (5/112,1909/5040,1249/2520,13/210,2/105). At least two vertices lie on a cycle so depth<=4, and an explicit rank matrix attains it. The full finite probability space, not an extrapolated sample, is exhausted for precisely 3×3 games. This says nothing about arbitrary play protocols or larger matrices.
